A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedCRP-CL research and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on 16 tasks, baseline comparisons, ablations, robustness evaluations, and additional empirical results in Appendices E, F, and H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including segmentation and forgetting measurements in Tables 2–3 and supplementary results in Appendices E, F, and H.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical CRP modality discovery, prompt embeddings, modality-specific LoRA adapters, intra-modality EWC, and training objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 16 tasks across endoscopy, dermoscopy, ultrasound, and chest X-ray imaging. Dataset coverage and prompt perturbation scenarios remain unchanged in Table 1, Section 4.4, and Appendices B and G.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain Individual, Sequential, EWC, RAPF, CL-LoRA, and MoE-Adapters. Comparison methods in the modality-grouping, clustering, and encoder experiments are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, Dice and forgetting metrics, preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations, and four task orderings are identical. The supplementary evaluation procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component and loss ablations, order sensitivity, encoder and prompt robustness, cold-start assignment analysis, Gaussian stabilization analysis, and Fisher-weighted adapter merging experiments.

E5.justification: The mean-plus/minus reporting in Table 2 and standard-deviation bands across task orderings in Figure 3 are unchanged. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains MedCRP-CL's 73.3 ± 1.0% Dice and 4.1 ± 0.8% forgetting. All other numerical results and qualitative findings, including the appendix results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and equations are identical. Appendix A retains the same assumptions, clustering-consistency and forgetting-bound propositions, proofs, and implications.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about automatic semantic modality discovery, replay-free continual learning, reduced forgetting, and parameter efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality separation, knowledge transfer, and ablation results are unchanged. The stated dependence on suitable text encoders, failures under extreme prompt corruption, and clinical-validation qualifications are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, hyperparameters, prompt templates, dataset descriptions, and task sequences are identical. The code and model-resource URLs remain unchanged; bibliography metadata additions provide no new implementation information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Updated DOI, proceedings, page, and capitalization information refers to existing references rather than adding works or revising relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds DOIs to the Chen et al. and Gao–Morel references, expands proceedings metadata and TRACE's page range, and standardizes several reference-title capitalizations. The arXiv version stamp changes; research prose and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Expanded reference entries cause limited line and spacing reflow on bibliography pages 10–11, and the first-page version stamp changes. All six figures and eighteen tables retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies fuller metadata and standardized names for already identifiable references. This small editorial cleanup leaves the scientific explanation, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, producing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
